home.headline: This is NATL.
home.lede: I'm Arslan. I built a short YAML runner for web UI and API — so you can write the test once and keep it when the stack moves.

home.title: Home
home.html:
Hi — I'm Arslan, and I built NATL because I was tired of rewriting the same smoke tests every time the stack changed.

This is a short open-source YAML runner for web UI and API. You write one compact scenario. You run it locally or in CI. When the team swaps Playwright for something else, you change engine: — not the whole suite.

If you're new here: take the course. Don't skim the canon first. Canon is for after you've seen a green PASS.

Course

Lectures 0–8 + a problem set. This is the front door.

Syntax

Full language map — every field and verb I support.

Troubleshooting

When it fails (and it will), start here before you blame YAML.

Adapters

Playwright by default. Selenium and Cypress when you need them.

Install in one breath

npm install -g @natl/cli @natl/adapter-playwright
npx playwright install chromium
natl --version

Then open the course. I'll meet you in Lecture 0.

Links

  • GitHub
  • npm @natl/cli
  • examples/ — scenarios I keep in the repo

getting-started.title: Course
getting-started.html:
Course

Welcome. I'm Arslan, and this is how I teach NATL — the path I wish someone had walked me through.

You will install the runner, earn a green PASS, then learn the language piece by piece: UI, variables, config, page objects, data-driven rows, HTTP, and control flow. By the end you should be able to write a real smoke suite without guessing.

Expect roughly an evening of focused work. Skim the syllabus, then do the lectures in order. The Syntax page is the full reference — come back to it often.

Syllabus

  1. Lecture 0 — Setup & first PASS
  2. Lecture 1 — Anatomy of a scenario
  3. Lecture 2 — UI steps & asserts
  4. Lecture 3 — Vars, secrets, project config
  5. Lecture 4 — Page objects (do:)
  6. Lecture 5 — Data-driven cases:
  7. Lecture 6 — HTTP & with: http
  8. Lecture 7 — Flow: if / for / repeat / parallel
  9. Lecture 8 — Tags, retries, CLI filters
  10. Problem set

Lecture 0 — Setup & first PASS

Goal: see ✓ PASS on a real scenario I already wrote.

You need: Node.js 18+, a terminal, about fifteen minutes.

npm install -g @natl/cli @natl/adapter-playwright
npx playwright install chromium
natl --version

Clone the repo and run the login fixture (local HTML — no flaky public site):

git clone https://github.com/arslan-ahmetjanov/natl.git
cd natl/examples
natl run login.yaml

That feeling when it passes? Keep it. Everything else in this course is more of that.

Try this: break the assert text on purpose, run again, read the FAIL line (file + step). Fix it. Learning starts when you break things safely.

Lecture 1 — Anatomy of a scenario

Open examples/login.yaml with me:

name: Login smoke
engine: playwright
tags: [smoke]
vars:
  base_url: ./fixtures/shop.html
  user: demo@test.com
  pass: secret
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - fill: "#email"
    with: $user
  - fill: "#password"
    with: $pass
  - click: "#login-btn"
  - assert: ".welcome"
    text: "Добро пожаловать"

Top to bottom:

  • name — what you see in the report
  • engine — how we drive the browser (playwright by default; also selenium, cypress, or http)
  • tags — optional labels for --tags
  • vars — values you reference as $user
  • steps — the script

Other root fields you'll meet soon: timeout, retries, secrets, imports, cases, before_each / after_each, elements, actions, locator_strategy, data. Full list → Syntax.

Scaffold your own project when you're ready to leave my fixtures:

mkdir my-tests && cd my-tests
natl init
natl run tests/

Lecture 2 — UI steps & asserts

I designed the verbs so a smoke fits on one screen. Primary rhythm: target + check.

- goto: $base_url
- fill: "#email"
  with: $user
- select: "#country"
  with: "KZ"
- check: "#agree"
- click: "#submit"          # tap: is the same step
- assert: ".ok"
  text: "Done"
- assert: ".ok"
  contains: "Do"
- assert: ".banner"
  visible: true
- assert: ".banner"
  attr: class contains "active"
- assert: current_url contains "/dashboard"

Auto-wait: actions and asserts wait for the target within timeout. You usually do not need wait: ".ok visible" before an assert.

Keep explicit wait: for delays (wait: 500), hidden / attached / detached, or unusual timing.

Soft failures (collect, don't stop):

- assert: ".price"
  text: "$10"
  soft: true
# alias:
- soft_assert: ".stock"
  visible: true

Capture & extract when you need a value later:

- get_text: ".title"
  save: page_title
- get_attr: "#link"
  attr: href
  save: href
- screenshot:
    file: artifacts/after-login.png
    full_page: true
- set: $total = $price * $qty
- log: "total=$total"

Gestures (same scenario for desktop and mobile web — no if: mobile):

- scroll: "#footer"
  into_view: true
- swipe: "#carousel"
  direction: left
- long_press: "#card"
  duration_ms: 700

Try this: run examples/soft_assert_demo.yaml and examples/gestures_demo.yaml.

Lecture 3 — Vars, secrets, project config

$name comes from vars (and from case rows, includes, POM calls). Nested: $order.id.

Secrets from the environment — never commit real passwords:

secrets:
  env:
    file: .env

vars:
  user: $env.TEST_USER
  pass: $secret.TEST_PASS

$env.KEY and $secret.KEY read the same store; secrets are masked in logs. See examples/env_login.yaml.

Project defaults live in natl.config.yaml:

engine: playwright
browser: chromium
timeout: 15000
base_url: https://staging.example.com
headless: true
artifacts_dir: artifacts
retries: 0
trace: on-fail
video: off

Stands without copying URLs into every file:

config/staging.yaml
config/prod.yaml

natl run tests/ --env staging
natl run tests/ --config config/prod.yaml

Merge order (highest wins): CLI flags → test YAML → env profile → natl.config → defaults.

Lecture 4 — Page objects (do:)

Put selectors and named flows in a page file. Call them from the scenario.

# pages/login.yaml
elements:
  email: "#email"
  password: "#password"
  submit: "#login-btn"
actions:
  login:
    - fill: $email
      with: $user
    - fill: $password
      with: $pass
    - click: $submit

# pom_login.yaml
imports:
  - pages/login.yaml
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - do: login.login
    user: $user
    pass: $pass

do: page.action is the happy path. include: login/login is the lower-level form (file or whole-file reuse). Sibling keys on do: merge into the action scope.

Locator strategy lives on config / page / element — not on every step. Web today: css, xpath.

elements:
  title:
    strategy: xpath
    value: "//h1"

Try this: natl run pom_login.yaml from examples/.

Lecture 5 — Data-driven cases:

One scenario, many rows. Each row merges into vars and runs steps once.

name: Data-driven login
cases:
  - { name: user1, user: "a@test.com", pass: secret, expect: "Welcome, A" }
  - { name: user2, user: "b@test.com", pass: secret, expect: "Welcome, B" }
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - fill: "#email"
    with: $user
  - fill: "#password"
    with: $pass
  - click: "#login-btn"
  - assert: ".welcome"
    text: $expect

Report names look like Data-driven login [user1]. Use name or label on the row; otherwise [case N].

For nested or computed loops, use data: + for: (next lecture). Prefer cases: for simple tables.

Try this: natl run data_driven.yaml.

Lecture 6 — HTTP & with: http

API-only scenario:

engine: http
vars:
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8765
steps:
  - get: $base_url/get
    save: ping
  - post: $base_url/post
    body: { hello: world }
    headers: { X-Test: "1" }
    save: echo
  - assert: $echo.status == 200
  - assert: $echo.ok == true

Verbs: get / post / put / patch / delete. Saved value: { status, headers, body, ok }. Legacy api: still works — prefer the verbs.

UI + API in one file — switch context with a block (not a per-step engine:):

engine: playwright
steps:
  - goto: $base_url
  - with: http
    steps:
      - get: $api_base/get
        save: ping
      - assert: $ping.status == 200
  - click: "#refresh"

My HTTP demos need the local stub first:

node stubs/echo-server.mjs
# other terminal:
natl run http_only.yaml
natl run ui_http_block.yaml

Lecture 7 — Flow: if / for / repeat / parallel

- if: $role == "admin"
  then:
    - click: "#admin"
  else:
    - click: "#user"

- for: $item in $data
  steps:
    - log: $item.name

- for: $i in range(1, 3)
  steps:
    - log: "i=$i"

- repeat: 3
  steps:
    - click: "#next"   # sets $i each time

- repeat:
    until: $done == true
  steps:
    - click: "#poll"

- parallel:
    - get: $api/a
      save: a
    - get: $api/b
      save: b

before_each / after_each run around steps on every attempt (including retries).

Expressions: == != > < >= <= contains matches and or not. Builtins include now, today, random_*, len, trim, upper, lower, range, and more — see Syntax → Expressions.

Lecture 8 — Tags, retries, CLI filters

name: Checkout
tags: [smoke, checkout]
retries: 1
natl run tests/ --tags smoke
natl run tests/ --tags smoke,auth
natl run tests/ --grep "Login"
natl run tests/ --retries 2
natl run suite.yaml --engine selenium
natl run suite.yaml --headed

--tags is OR. Combined with --grep → AND. Zero matches → exit 1.

Retries re-run the whole scenario with a fresh browser context. Last attempt wins; JSON may mark flaky: true.

Problem set

  1. From examples/, get login.yaml, pom_login.yaml, and data_driven.yaml green.
  2. natl init a new folder. Point base_url at a page you care about. Write a three-step smoke.
  3. Extract selectors into pages/ and call them with do:.
  4. Add a with: http block that checks a health endpoint (use the echo stub if you need one).
  5. Tag it smoke and run with --tags smoke.

When you're stuck — Troubleshooting. When you need every field — Syntax.

This is the course. I'll keep teaching as the language grows. — Arslan

syntax.title: Syntax
syntax.html:
Syntax

This is the full language map — every public field and verb I support today. The Course teaches it in order; this page is what you keep open while writing.

Source of truth in the repo: schemas under @natl/core + the interpreter. If docs and runtime disagree, trust the runtime and open an issue.

On this page

  1. Root fields
  2. Project config & env profiles
  3. UI steps
  4. Assert
  5. Extract, set, log, screenshot
  6. Gestures
  7. HTTP
  8. POM
  9. Cases & data
  10. Flow
  11. Vars, secrets, expressions
  12. CLI filters
  13. Compact form & sugar

Root fields (scenario YAML)

FieldMeaning
nameDisplay name (reports, --grep)
tagsString list for --tags
engineplaywright | selenium | cypress | http
timeoutDefault step timeout (ms)
retriesExtra full-scenario attempts after failure
varsScenario variables ($name)
secretsHow to load secrets (see below)
importsPage / shared YAML paths
elementsPOM locators
actionsPOM named step lists
locator_strategyDefault for string selectors (css | xpath)
casesData-driven rows
dataArray exposed as $data for for:
before_each / after_eachHooks around steps each attempt
stepsMain step list

Every step may also carry: timeout, save, debug. To switch engines mid-scenario, use a with: block — that is what the runtime honors.

Project config & env profiles

natl.config.yaml (nearest walking up from the test file):

engine: playwright
browser: chromium          # adapter-specific
timeout: 15000
base_url: https://staging.example.com
headless: true
viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }
locator_strategy: css
artifacts_dir: artifacts
retries: 0
trace: on-fail             # off | on | on-fail
video: off
soft_assert_screenshot: false

Env profiles: config/<name>.yaml via --env staging, or any overlay via --config path.yaml (mutually exclusive).

Merge priority: CLI → test YAML → env profile → base config → defaults.

UI steps

VerbForm
gotogoto: $url or goto: { url, timeout } — http(s), file://, or relative → file
click / tapSame step; prefer click:
fillfill: "#id" + sibling with:
selectlocator + with: (option value)
check / unchecklocator
waitms, or selector + visible|hidden|attached|detached

Auto-wait: actions and asserts wait for the target within timeout. Prefer assert over a redundant wait: … visible.

Assert

- assert: ".welcome"
  text: "Hello"            # or is:
- assert: ".welcome"
  contains: "Hell"
- assert: $welcome
  visible: true
- assert: ".banner"
  hidden: true
- assert: ".price"
  attr: class contains "sale"
- assert: current_url == "https://example.com/app"
- assert: current_url contains "/app"
- assert: $ping.status == 200
- assert: ".price"
  text: "$10"
  soft: true
- soft_assert: ".stock"    # alias → soft: true
  visible: true

Attr operators inline: ==, !=, contains, matches.

Soft asserts collect failures; the run fails at the end. Hard assert is fail-fast.

Extract, set, log, screenshot

- get_text: ".title"
  save: title
- get_attr: "a"
  attr: href
  save: href
- set: $total = $price * $qty
- log: "hello"
- log: { message: "x", level: warn }   # info|debug|warn|error
- debug: true
- screenshot:
    file: artifacts/shot.png
    full_page: true

Gestures

- scroll: "#footer"
  into_view: true          # or delta_x / delta_y
- swipe: "#carousel"
  direction: left          # left|right|up|down
  distance: 200
- long_press: "#card"
  duration_ms: 700

Same steps for desktop and mobile web. Touch fidelity = adapter capability.

HTTP

engine: http
steps:
  - get: $base_url/health
    save: ping
  - post: $base_url/login
    headers: { Authorization: "Bearer $token" }
    body: { user: $user }
    save: resp
  - put: …
  - patch: …
  - delete: …
  - assert: $resp.status == 200

Saved shape: { status, headers, body, ok }. Relative URLs resolve against vars.base_url when it is http(s).

Mix with UI:

- with: http
  steps:
    - get: $api/orders/$id
      save: order

Legacy api: still parses; new work should use the verbs above.

POM

# pages/login.yaml
locator_strategy: css
elements:
  email: "#email"
  title:
    strategy: xpath
    value: "//h1"
actions:
  login:
    - fill: $email
      with: $user
    - click: "#login-btn"

# scenario
imports:
  - pages/login.yaml
steps:
  - do: login.login
    user: $user
    pass: $pass
  - include: login/login   # path-style / whole-file
    vars: { user: $user }

Page files may omit steps (only elements + actions). natl run tests/ skips pages/ and config/ directories.

Strategy priority for an element: object strategy → page locator_strategy → project → css.

Cases & data

cases:
  - { name: a, user: a@test.com, expect: "A" }
  - { label: b, user: b@test.com, expect: "B" }
steps:
  - fill: "#email"
    with: $user
  - assert: ".hi"
    text: $expect

data:
  - { name: one }
  - { name: two }
steps:
  - for: $item in $data
    steps:
      - log: $item.name

Prefer cases: for simple tables; data: + for: for nested / computed loops.

Flow

- if: $role == "admin"
  then:
    - click: "#admin"
  else:
    - click: "#user"

- for: $i in range(1, 5)
  steps:
    - log: $i

- repeat: 3                 # or "3 times" / times: 3
  steps:
    - click: "#next"        # sets $i

- repeat:
    until: $done == true
  steps:
    - click: "#poll"        # max 1000 iterations

- parallel:                 # wait: all (default) | any
  - get: $api/a
    save: a
  - get: $api/b
    save: b

- parallel:
    wait: any
    steps:
      - get: $api/fast
      - get: $api/slow

Vars, secrets, expressions

SyntaxMeaning
$userVariable
$order.idNested field
$env.KEYEnvironment / .env (missing → error)
$secret.KEYSame store; masked in logs
${ENV:KEY}Legacy compat
 
secrets:
  env:
    file: .env
    encoding: utf-8

Operators: == != > < >= <= contains matches and or not.

Builtins: now, today, random_int, random_string, random_uuid, random_email, len, contains, trim, upper, lower, replace, match, join, map, filter, range.

Runtime injects current_url for URL asserts / expressions.

CLI filters

natl run tests/ --tags smoke,auth    # OR
natl run tests/ --grep "Login"       # RegExp on name or path
natl run tests/ --retries 2
natl run tests/ --env staging
natl run tests/ --headed
natl run tests/ --engine selenium
natl run tests/ --trace on-fail
natl run tests/ --video off

--tags and --grep combine with AND. Zero matches → exit 1.

Compact form & sugar

Primary (what you should commit — valid YAML):

- fill: "#email"
  with: $user
- wait: ".dashboard visible"
- assert: ".welcome"
  text: "Hello"

Runtime sugar (preprocessor; IDEs may flag as invalid YAML):

- fill: "#email" with: $user
- assert: ".welcome" text: "Hello"
- scroll: $footer into_view

Nested objects (fill: { locator, with }, …) are valid for tooling.

IDE: wire @natl/core schemas via the YAML extension yaml.schemas — see the CLI README.

— Arslan

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.html:
Troubleshooting

When something breaks, I look here before I rewrite the scenario. You should too.

natl: command not found

npm install -g @natl/cli @natl/adapter-playwright
npm prefix -g
natl --version

Browser / Chromium errors

npx playwright install chromium
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

FAIL … assert / element not found

  • Is the selector still right?
  • Prefer stable #id over long CSS chains
  • Check the screenshot under artifacts/

YAML indentation

- fill: "#email"
  with: $user

HTTP examples hang or fail

node stubs/echo-server.mjs
natl run http_only.yaml

Wrong engine / adapter missing

natl engines
npm install -g @natl/adapter-playwright

Still stuck? Open an issue on GitHub with the FAIL line and your OS.

— Arslan

adapters.title: Adapters
adapters.html:
Adapters

The YAML is the contract. Adapters drive a browser — or skip it for HTTP.

enginePackageWhen I pick it
playwright@natl/adapter-playwrightDefault. New projects. CI.
selenium@natl/adapter-seleniumExisting WebDriver / Grid
cypress@natl/adapter-cypressCypress-heavy teams (MVP bridge)
httpbuilt into @natl/coreAPI-only scenarios
 
engine: playwright
browser: chromium
headless: true
natl run suite.yaml --engine selenium

UI + HTTP in one file → with: http (see the course, Lecture 6).

Browsers are an adapter capability — not a hard-coded matrix in the language.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.html:
Architecture

Mental model I draw on a whiteboard:

  • You write YAML — what to test
  • @natl/cli — finds files, loads config, filters tags
  • @natl/core — parses, interpolates, runs the interpreter
  • Adapter — Playwright / Selenium / Cypress — or built-in http

Typical flows stay portable when you change engine:. Rare edges live in the canon.

canon.title: Canon
canon.html:
Canon

These aren't slogans. They're the rules I refuse to break while growing NATL.

I believeSo
Short languageA smoke fits on one screen
UI + API togetherwith: http in the same file
Context outside stepsconfig / --env / cases: — not if: mobile everywhere
Portable via adaptersSame YAML; browsers = adapter capability
Honest ceiling~90% of smokes; escape hatches for the rest
Runner ≠ TMSCLI runs tests — no dashboard product

— Arslan
